items.title: Pope Leo holds first Mass of South America tour in Uruguay
items.why: About 40,000 people attended Pope Leo XIV's Mass in the rain in Paysandú, western Uruguay, on Saturday, the Vatican says. It is the first papal visit to Uruguay in nearly four decades; the 12-day tour continues to Argentina and Peru.
items.matters: The trip had been in doubt after the 71-year-old pope's lung cancer surgery last month.

items.title: US sets up task force to block Iran's land supply routes
items.why: US Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday to stop weapons and sanctioned goods crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. The same day, it says, a US aircraft disabled a St Kitts-flagged cargo ship trying to break its naval blockade in the Gulf of Oman.
items.matters: It extends a months-long US naval blockade of Iranian ports to Iran's land borders.

items.changed: Updated: police raised the toll to at least six; the prime minister calls it terrorism
items.title: At least six killed in Krakow shooting, which Poland's PM calls terrorism
items.why: A gunman fired from a car in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, killing at least six people and wounding about 15, police say. Officers shot and detained the suspect, a Polish man; three more bodies were found at his home.
items.matters: The interior minister says the suspect held ultra-nationalist views; Poland has declared two days of mourning.

items.title: Heavy rain floods tens of thousands of tents in Gaza
items.why: The first winter storm of the season flooded at least 70,000 tents sheltering displaced people across Gaza on Saturday, the Hamas-run government media office says. The civil defence agency says it received about 1,500 distress calls and lacks the equipment to respond. No deaths have been reported.
items.matters: Local officials say Gaza urgently needs prefabricated homes, tents and heating as winter begins.

items.title: New Zealand beat Tonga 34-10 to reach Rugby League World Cup final
items.why: New Zealand's Kiwis beat Tonga 34-10 in Newcastle, Australia, on Saturday, after trailing 10-6 in the first half. It is their first World Cup final since 2013. They will play Australia or Samoa in Brisbane next Sunday.
items.matters: New Zealand's women's team, the Kiwi Ferns, also reached their final, beating Samoa 32-0.

items.title: New Zealand election too close to call after election-night count
items.why: With all polling places counted after Saturday's election, National has about 29.4% and Labour 29.2%, RNZ reports. National and its partners ACT and NZ First are projected to win a one-seat majority. About 700,000 special votes are still to be counted; final results are due on 27 November.
items.matters: The centrist Opportunity Party has entered parliament and could hold the balance of power.

items.title: Towhid Hridoy scores 242, Bangladesh's highest Test innings
items.why: Towhid Hridoy made 242 not out against West Indies in Sylhet, passing Mushfiqur Rahim's 219 not out from 2018. His innings took Bangladesh from 184 for 7 to 386, a first-innings lead over West Indies' 356.
items.matters: He is only the fourth Bangladesh batter to score a Test double century.

items.title: Pakistani astronaut to be first foreigner on China's space station
items.why: China's Manned Space Agency says a Pakistani astronaut will fly on the Shenzhou-24 mission as a payload specialist, Chinese state media reported on Saturday. The astronaut, not yet named, will make a short stay and return on Shenzhou-23. No launch date has been given.
items.matters: It would be the first time China's crewed space programme has flown a foreign astronaut.

items.title: Russian missiles hit Kyiv's power supply and a major bridge
items.why: Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones overnight into Saturday, mostly at Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukraine says. Strikes damaged the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro and substations carrying power from two nuclear plants. Officials say at least one person was killed and several injured.
items.matters: It comes days before US-backed talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday.

items.changed: Updated: Peña is under house arrest and Pedro Alliana has been sworn in.
items.title: Paraguay's Senate removes President Peña, who is put under house arrest
items.why: All 44 senators present voted on Friday to remove Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, which locked nearly half of Paraguayans out of their savings. Prosecutors then put him under house arrest over alleged breach of trust; Peña denies wrongdoing. Vice-President Pedro Alliana was sworn in.
items.matters: Alliana will serve until August 2028; deposit insurance covers 97% of Ueno's customers, the central bank says.

items.title: Polar vortex weakens weeks earlier than ever recorded
items.why: The polar vortex, a ring of cold winds high above the Arctic, is breaking down earlier than ever recorded, forecasters at the ECMWF told AFP. It usually peaks around January. The UK Met Office calls it exceptional but says it does not mean a cold spell is certain.
items.matters: An early breakdown raises the chance of cold snaps in Europe, North America and East Asia later in November and December.

items.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff
items.why: President Donald Trump said on Friday that Stephen Miller, 41, his deputy chief of staff and the architect of his immigration crackdown, will replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff from Monday. Wiles is moving to Trump's political operation. The change follows Republican losses in Tuesday's midterms.
items.matters: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called Miller an extremist; the White House calls him one of Trump's most trusted advisers.

items.title: US measles cases pass 5,000, the most in 35 years
items.why: The US has recorded 5,182 confirmed measles cases so far in 2026, the CDC said on Friday, more than double last year's 2,289 and the most since 1991. About 96% of cases are in people who are unvaccinated or whose status is unknown. States report at least eight deaths.
items.matters: The US is expected to lose its measles-elimination status, held since 2000, at a regional health meeting next week.

items.title: US economy adds 165,000 jobs in October, far more than expected
items.why: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against forecasts of about 65,000, and unemployment fell to 4.1%, the Labor Department said on Friday. Earlier months were revised up by 84,000. Average pay rose 3.1% over the year, less than inflation.
items.matters: Strong hiring makes a Federal Reserve interest rate rise in December more likely, economists say.

items.title: Tesla to stop making the Cybertruck in Texas from mid-2027
items.why: Elon Musk said on Friday that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around mid-2027, to make room for its Cybercab robotaxi. US Cybertruck sales fell 48% in 2025 to about 20,000, far below the 250,000 a year Musk once predicted.
items.matters: Musk says existing Cybertrucks will stay on the road; it is unclear whether production will move elsewhere.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats spread from European flights to newsrooms
items.why: Ireland's RTÉ evacuated its Dublin headquarters on Friday after an emailed bomb threat, and Bulgaria's Nova TV and Britain's Sky also received threats, Reuters reports. More flights were escorted or searched across Europe. No explosives have been found and every plane landed safely.
items.matters: No government has said who is behind the week of threats; Russia denies involvement.

items.changed: Updated: Herzog chose Eisenkot on Saturday
items.title: Israel's president asks Eisenkot, not Netanyahu, to form a government
items.why: President Isaac Herzog chose former army chief Gadi Eisenkot on Saturday after parties with 67 of the Knesset's 120 seats backed him. Eisenkot's bloc won 48 seats in the 27 October election; he has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to build a coalition.
items.matters: Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister; if no coalition can be formed, Israel faces another election.

items.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
items.why: A jury at Southwark Crown Court in London found comedian Russell Brand, 51, guilty on Thursday of one rape and three sexual assaults between 2004 and 2009. He was cleared of two other rape charges and one other charge. He denied all of them and is in custody.
items.matters: The judge said a significant prison sentence is inevitable; sentencing is due on Monday.
